Tourne Cruise Edition Is a European All-Rounder Camper Van Built for All-Season Travel
24 photos
Photo: Tourne Campervans
The most appreciated camper vans for remote travel are those that combine everyday drivability with practicality, smart comfort, and self-sufficiency, and the Tourne Cruise Edition seems to check all of these boxes.
Built in Europe by Tourne Campervans, a small manufacturer based in Pivka, Slovenia, that specializes in hand-assembled, all-season-ready van conversions, the Tourne Cruise Edition is a four-berth camper that is fitted out for maximum comfort on the road. It combines a carefully planned interior with practical equipment aimed at making everyday touring comfortable, guaranteeing memorable travel experiences.
The Cruise Edition is one of the three models offered by Tourne Campervans, alongside the Tourne Expre and the Tourne Select. While the Tourne Expre is the entry-level option that offers an accessible starting point for all-season travel, the Tourne Select is the flagship model, featuring higher-end cabinetry and finishes, improved off-grid capabilities, and a more comprehensive cab technology package.
The Tourne Cruise is the mid-tier all-rounder and is the most popular model in the company’s lineup. It is offered as a pre-equipped camper van, with features that the team chose based on what their clients used the most in the past. As such, it provides all the essentials for convenient travels, while still leaving room for some optional extras.
Photo: Tourne Campervans Based on a Fiat Ducato chassis, the Cruise Edition camper van is available in two lengths. There is a 6-meter (19.7-foot) version and a 6.4-meter (21-foot) one, with the latter offering some extra living space and storage. The base vehicle uses a 2.2-liter Euro 6.4 diesel engine delivering 140 hp or 180 hp, paired with manual or automatic transmissions, depending on the chosen configuration.
For the exterior finish, white is the standard color, but clients can choose between several other options, including different shades of gray, black, blue and green. Designed to remain stealthy, the exterior is rather unadorned, with just the extra windows, a Thule awning, and the solar panel on the roof pointing at its camper identity.
The Cruise Edition comes with a painted front bumper, black skid plates, and full LED headlights, which is quite important when traveling at night. A Dometic Raintec RT100 outdoor light with rain cover and remote control is also installed on the passenger side, and an entry step makes getting in and out easier. The van rides on 16" alloy aluminum diamond black wheels and also comes equipped with a Monoblock towing hitch at the rear, an outdoor shower, and an external gas connection.
For the van’s interior, Tourne’s design approach focuses on Scandinavian-inspired simplicity, durability and practical use of space . The color scheme includes neutral tones, and all the furniture and cabinetry is made in the company’s own CNC facility using moisture-proof and scratch-resistant poplar panels and high-quality laminate protective surface layer. The end furniture strips are made of solid wood, and the furniture pieces are fitted with high-quality hardware.
Photo: Tourne Campervans An important thing that needs to be mentioned is that the company developed its camper van models in collaboration with Nordic partners, so they are built with year-round travel in mind. Features like high-performance elastomeric foam insulation, custom-fitted to the vehicle’s shape, diesel-powered heating, and integrated floor air channels designed to distribute warmth around the living area ensure you can travel comfortably in the Cruise in any season. An electric underfloor heating system can also be used when the van is connected to shore power.
In terms of layout, the Cruise Edition boasts an open-cab interior, with swiveling cab seats that become part of an extended seating area at the front. The swivel captain’s chairs pair with a two-passenger seatbelted bench and an adjustable table to create a nice dinette for four. A fifth person can join in, as there is also a small bench that slides out from inside the kitchen block.
The center of the van is occupied by a compact yet functional kitchen and an enclosed interior bathroom, while the rear of the van is dedicated to the main sleeping area. Instead of a fixed bed, the company opted for a modular Murphy-style bed, with removable cushions and a fold-away platform that opens up the garage area if you need more space for carrying bulky equipment.
Photo: Tourne Campervans One of the cleverest features inside the van is Tourne’s DREAM4 System, which allows the model to sleep up to four people without resorting to an elevator bed or a pop-top roof. This is a unique patented modular system that lets you transform the front dinette into another double bed measuring 185 by 120 cm (73 by 47 inches).
Though compact, the kitchen has more than enough storage and comes equipped with a two-burner gas hob, a sink, and a 90-liter refrigerator with a small freezer compartment. There is very little countertop for meal prep, but a flip-up extension and the front dining table come in handy in this regard.
Adding another layer of convenience , the indoor wet bathroom offers a shower, a small sink, a swivel toilet, and a wall-mounted cabinet for toiletries. It looks very sleek and modern, and is fully enclosed. Since we’re talking about the shower, it’s worth mentioning that the van’s water system includes a 95-liter (25-gallon) fresh water tank and a 100-liter (26-gallon) waste water tank.
There is also a roof vent in the bathroom, helping with ventilation after showering, and hangers and a rod lets you dry your clothes in here as well.
Photo: Tourne Campervans The rear bedroom fits an east-to-west bed measuring 190 by 140 cm (75 by 55 inches) in the 6-meter Cruise model, while the 6.4 version allows for a north-to-south bed measuring 190 by 190 cm (75 by 75 inches). There are overhead cabinets and small shelves on both sides of the van, providing plenty of space for clothes and personal belongings.
The camper van’s standard electrical system includes a 100Ah lithium battery, a 140-watt solar panel, and a 220A alternator, offering enough power to go around and explore. But if you want to spend more time in off-grid locations, you can upgrade the system with 300 Ah of extra battery capacity, a portable Shadow Flux solar panel module with external connection socket, and up to 2000W inverter.
The list of optional features also includes a Telair roof air conditioner, additional underbody protection, a Thule bike rack for two bikes, a steel spare wheel, and more.
The starting price for the Tourne Cruise camper van is €64,900 ($71,200), but that’s before adding any optional packages. A fully equipped unit with additional equipment like solar panels, awning, outdoor shower, and chassis upgrades can come in at over €82,300 ($90,825).
